newsitem.title: USA: Judge to rule on O.J. Simpson's request for new trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge to rule on O.J. Simpson's request for new trial.

text.p: The judge who presided over O.J. Simpson's wrongful death civil trial was scheduled to rule on Monday on Simpson's request for a new trial.

Simpson, who was found liable in February for the deaths of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend, Ronald Goldman, was seeking to have that verdict set aside on the grounds of jury misconduct and newly discovered evidence.

Also on Monday, Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki will rule on Simpson's motion to reduce the size of the $33.5 million civil verdict. The civil trial jury ordered Simpson to pay $25 million in punitive damages to the Brown and Goldman families and another $8.5 million in compensatory damages to the Goldmans.

Simpson, a former football star and television personality, was acquitted of the murders in 1995 after a lengthy criminal trial. But he was found liable for the deaths and ordered to pay damages by a civil jury after the victims' families sued for wrongful death.
In March, sheriff's deputies began removing art, jewels and other items from Simpson's estate to satisfy part of the judgment against him.
